input:
AI infrastructure spending is going to keep compounding for at least another
   two years. The constraint isn't demand, it's power and packaging capacity, and
   the companies that own those bottlenecks capture the margin. I want exposure to
   that but I don't want to be wiped out if the capex cycle turns.

thesis.title: AI Infrastructure Bottleneck: Power & Packaging
thesis.summary: AI capex is demand-pull, not hype-push, and the binding constraints are power delivery and advanced packaging — not GPUs or software. NVDA owns the GPU stack but also benefits from CoWoS packaging scarcity. AVGO designs custom silicon that bypasses NVDA entirely and sits inside the same packaging bottleneck. MSFT and AMZN are the hyperscalers whose capex guidance is the clearest leading indicator of whether the cycle continues. QQQx and SPYx provide the defensive floor so a capex reversal doesn't wipe the position. This is a levered-but-hedged expression of the bottleneck thesis.

holdings.rationale: Primary beneficiary of AI training demand and CoWoS advanced packaging scarcity. If packaging capacity is the binding constraint, NVDA's allocation of that capacity is a direct margin lever. Sized large because no other single name captures the bottleneck as cleanly, but kept below 2500 to avoid single-name wipeout risk.

Custom ASIC silicon for Google TPUs and Meta's MTIA runs through the same advanced packaging supply chain. AVGO captures margin on chips that don't compete with NVDA, diversifying the packaging thesis without duplicating GPU exposure.

Azure capex is the most transparent hyperscaler signal available. MSFT guides capex explicitly each quarter; a flat or down guide is the clearest early warning that the cycle is turning. Held at 1000 bps as a thesis-signal holding, not pure return play.

Core defensive anchor. If the capex cycle turns, single-name AI names drop hard and fast; QQQx cushions that without abandoning tech exposure entirely. Sized at 3000 to keep core weight in the required band while providing meaningful downside buffer.

Broadens the defensive floor beyond tech-heavy QQQx. A capex reversal that hits AI names hard may spare non-tech S&P constituents; SPYx captures that optionality while keeping the basket mintable if AI names gap down simultaneously.

falsifier.claim: Hyperscaler capex continues to grow year-over-year for at least two consecutive quarters, confirming that demand — not sentiment — is driving AI infrastructure build-out.
falsifier.observable: Combined capex guidance from MSFT and AMZN at their next two quarterly earnings calls, reported in their investor relations filings.
falsifier.breachCondition: Either MSFT or AMZN guides capex flat or down year-over-year in two consecutive quarters, or both guide flat/down in the same quarter.
